disclaimer: Seed catalog for Aranya, not legal advice and not exhaustive. Items marked "source_cited" were checked against the cited primary source on 2026-11-03; items marked "verify" or "unverified" must still be confirmed against primary sources (Gazette of India, indiacode.nic.in, environmentclearance.nic.in, greentribunal.gov.in, the SCC/official reports) by a qualified person before use in any court-facing document.

instruments.label: National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
instruments.note: Enacted 2 June 2010; in force 18 October 2010. Amended by the Finance Act 2017 and the Tribunals Reforms Act 2021 (per the India Code consolidated text).

instruments.label: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986
instruments.note: Enacted 23 May 1986. Parent statute for the EIA and CRZ notifications (s.3).

instruments.label: Environmental Impact Assessment Notification, 2006
instruments.note: The official MoEFCC listing opens with S.O. 1533(E) of 14 September 2006 and runs through amendments to S.O. 3372(E) of 26 July 2023. The draft EIA Notification 2020 (released 12 March 2020) was NOT notified and is not law; never cite the 2020 draft as operative. Re-check the listing for amendments after 2023.

instruments.label: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
instruments.note: Renamed Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam by the Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act 2023 (reported in force 1 December 2023 - single secondary source; confirm the commencement notification).

instruments.label: Biological Diversity Act, 2002
instruments.note: Amended by the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act 2023 (assent 3 August 2023), brought into force 1 April 2024 by Gazette notification.

instruments.label: Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972
instruments.note: NOT listed in NGT Schedule I: harm arising only under this Act may fall outside the NGT's jurisdiction. Confirmed against Schedule I of the NGT Act.

instruments.label: Coastal Regulation Zone Notification, 2019
instruments.citation: G.S.R. 37(E), 18 January 2019, under EPA 1986 and the Environment (Protection) Rules 1986
instruments.note: Correct citation is G.S.R. 37(E) of 18 January 2019 - NOT S.O. 114(E), which was the 1991 CRZ notification. Supersedes the 2011 notification (S.O. 19(E)). Amended by S.O. 4886(E) of 26 Nov 2021 and S.O. 5495(E) of 24 Nov 2022; check for later amendments against the Gazette.

provisions.label: Tribunal to settle disputes
provisions.summary: Jurisdiction over all civil cases where a substantial question relating to the environment arises and the question arises out of the implementation of the enactments in Schedule I. An application must be made within six months of the date on which the cause of action first arose, extendable by up to sixty days for sufficient cause.
provisions.note: Six-month limitation (plus up to 60 days) confirmed against the Act text.

provisions.label: Relief, compensation and restitution
provisions.summary: The Tribunal may order (a) relief and compensation to victims of pollution and other environmental damage arising under the Schedule I enactments, (b) restitution of property damaged, and (c) restitution of the environment 'for such area or areas, as the Tribunal may think fit'. This relief is in addition to any relief under the Public Liability Insurance Act 1991.
provisions.note: Clause (c), restitution of the environment, is the statutory hook for restoration-scaled claims. Quoted verbatim from the Act.

provisions.label: Liability to pay relief or compensation
provisions.summary: Where death, injury, or damage to property or the environment results from an accident or the adverse impact of an activity, operation or process under a Schedule I enactment, the responsible person is liable to pay relief or compensation under the heads in Schedule II as the Tribunal determines; the Tribunal may apportion liability where it cannot be attributed to a single person.

provisions.label: Tribunal to apply certain principles
provisions.summary: The Tribunal shall, while passing any order, decision or award, apply the principles of sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the polluter pays principle.

provisions.label: Scheduled enactments (seven)
provisions.summary: [See ss.14(1), 15(1), 17(1)(a), 17(2), 19(4)(j), 34(1)] The seven enactments: (1) Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974; (2) Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Cess Act 1977; (3) Forest (Conservation) Act 1980; (4) Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1981; (5) Environment (Protection) Act 1986; (6) Public Liability Insurance Act 1991; (7) Biological Diversity Act 2002.
provisions.note: Enumeration confirmed verbatim against the Act. The Wild Life (Protection) Act 1972 is not in Schedule I.

provisions.label: Heads of compensation and relief
provisions.summary: [See ss.15(4) and 17(1)] Heads under which compensation or relief may be claimed, including death, disability, loss of wages, medical expenses, damage to private property, government relief expenses, and head (g): expenses incurred by the Government for administrative or legal action or to cope with harm or damage, 'including compensation for environmental degradation and restoration of the quality of the environment', plus losses to government and harm to fauna.
provisions.note: Head (g), covering restoration of the quality of the environment, is where a REA/HEA-scaled figure would sit. Quoted verbatim.

provisions.label: Power of Central Government to take measures
provisions.summary: The Central Government may take all such measures as it deems necessary or expedient to protect and improve the quality of the environment (s.3(1)); s.3(2) enumerates specific powers and s.3(3) allows constitution of authorities. This is the source of authority for the EIA Notification 2006 and the CRZ Notification.
provisions.note: General power confirmed; read s.3(1)-(3) for the specific sub-clause relied on in a given matter.

provisions.label: EC appraisal stages
provisions.summary: Paragraph 7 provides four stages for prior environmental clearance: (1) Screening (only for Category B, to decide B1/B2), (2) Scoping (Terms of Reference), (3) Public Consultation (public hearing plus written responses), and (4) Appraisal by the Expert Appraisal Committee (Category A, MoEFCC) or State EAC (Category B, SEIAA), leading to grant or refusal with conditions. The stages are sequential and not all apply to every project.
provisions.note: Four-stage structure of para 7 confirmed. Separately verify: the Supreme Court in Vanashakti v. Union of India (2025) is reported to have restricted post-facto environmental clearances; confirm before advising on ex post facto ECs.

doctrines.label: Polluter pays principle
doctrines.summary: The polluter bears the cost of both compensation to victims and restoration of the degraded environment; part of Indian environmental law and expressly directed by NGT Act s.20.
doctrines.note: Leading authorities: Vellore Citizens (1996) 5 SCC 647 and Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action (1996) 3 SCC 212.

doctrines.label: Precautionary principle
doctrines.summary: Where there are threats of serious or irreversible damage, lack of full scientific certainty is not a reason to postpone preventive measures; the onus is on the developer to show its action is environmentally benign. Adopted as part of Indian law in Vellore Citizens.

doctrines.label: Public trust doctrine
doctrines.summary: The State holds natural resources (rivers, forests, air, ecologically fragile land) as trustee for the public and cannot abdicate that trust by transferring them to private ownership or use.
doctrines.note: M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath, (1997) 1 SCC 388 (Span Motel). Confirmed via the Supreme Court's 2002 order in the same matter (doc/1239689), which restates the 1997 public trust holding.

doctrines.label: Sustainable development
doctrines.summary: Development and environmental protection are to be balanced so that present needs are met without compromising future generations; adopted as the governing principle in Vellore Citizens.

cases.label: Vellore Citizens' Welfare Forum v. Union of India
cases.principle: Precautionary and polluter pays principles are part of Indian environmental law; sustainable development adopted.
cases.note: Decided 28 August 1996 (Kuldip Singh and K. Venkataswami JJ.); also AIR 1996 SC 2715. Concerned pollution of the river Palar by Vellore tanneries. Confirm pinpoints against the SCC report.

cases.label: Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India
cases.principle: Absolute liability of an enterprise carrying on a hazardous activity; polluter pays for remediation of the affected area (Bichhri).
cases.note: Decided 13 February 1996 (B.P. Jeevan Reddy J.); also AIR 1996 SC 1446. Confirm specific paragraph pinpoints against the SCC report before relying on them.

cases.label: M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath
cases.principle: Public trust doctrine is part of the law of India; the polluter must bear the cost of reversing the ecological damage caused.
cases.note: Decided 13 December 1996 (Kuldip Singh and S. Saghir Ahmad JJ.); Span Motel on the river Beas. doc/1239689 is the Supreme Court's 2002 order in the same petition restating the 1997 holding; confirm paragraph pinpoints against (1997) 1 SCC 388.

methodologies.label: Habitat Equivalency Analysis (HEA)
methodologies.summary: Sizes compensatory restoration by equating the discounted flow of habitat services lost through injury with the discounted service gains of a restoration project (discounted service-acre-years). Used in U.S. natural resource damage assessment under CERCLA/OPA.
methodologies.note: No documented NGT or Indian court use. Present only as a persuasive comparative methodology via foreign-authority-handler; the restoration-cost output sits under NGT s.15/s.17 and Schedule II head (g), which is a novel argument in India.

methodologies.label: Resource Equivalency Analysis (REA)
methodologies.summary: Variant of equivalency analysis that scales restoration against a specific resource service (for example fisheries production or recreational use) rather than habitat area. Distinct from HEA; the choice of method is itself part of the expert argument.
methodologies.note: No documented NGT or Indian court use. Keep distinct from HEA in any filing.
